sections.content: You know this from Unit 16. Ask the time with *Hány óra van?* A whole hour is the number before *óra*, and *óra* stays singular: *Hét óra van.* Half and quarter hours count toward the next hour and leave out *óra*: *fél tíz* is 9:30, *negyed tíz* is 9:15, *háromnegyed tíz* is 9:45. A part of the day can come first: *Reggel fél nyolc van.*

sections.title: Days and months
sections.content: A day takes *-n* to say when: *hétfőn, kedden, szerdán, csütörtökön, pénteken, szombaton*. *Vasárnap* takes no ending. A month takes *-ban* or *-ben*: *júniusban, októberben*. Go from the biggest time to the smallest, then the place and the verb: *Júniusban szombaton délután a parkban sétálunk.* Ask with *Mikor?*

items.english: On Saturday afternoon we walk in the park.
In June we rest at home.

sections.content: English counts from the hour before (“half past nine”), Hungarian toward the hour after: *fél tíz* is 9:30, not 10:30. And *szerda* lengthens its final vowel before the ending: *szerdán*.
